drugs.name: lisinopril
drugs.summary: DEMO RECORD. Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor used for blood pressure control and commonly discussed in CKD where albuminuria is present. Kidney function and potassium are generally monitored by a clinician after starting or changing therapy.
contraindications: history of angioedema with an ACE inhibitor
drugs.source: DEMO fixture (not a validated drug database)

drugs.name: losartan
drugs.summary: DEMO RECORD. Angiotensin receptor blocker acting on the same renin-angiotensin system as ACE inhibitors, commonly described as an alternative where an ACE inhibitor is not tolerated. Kidney function and potassium are generally monitored by a clinician.
drugs.source: DEMO fixture (not a validated drug database)

drugs.name: dapagliflozin
drugs.summary: DEMO RECORD. Sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitor. Originally a glucose-lowering agent, now also discussed in general references for kidney outcomes in CKD. An early, temporary reduction in eGFR after starting is commonly described as expected.
drugs.source: DEMO fixture (not a validated drug database)

drugs.name: furosemide
drugs.summary: DEMO RECORD. Loop diuretic used for fluid overload and oedema, commonly described as remaining effective at reduced levels of kidney function. Volume depletion and electrolyte disturbance are the considerations most often discussed.
drugs.source: DEMO fixture (not a validated drug database)

drugs.name: ibuprofen
drugs.summary: DEMO RECORD. NSAID used for pain, fever and inflammation, widely available without prescription. Consistently flagged in general CKD references because NSAIDs are described as reducing prostaglandin-supported blood flow within the kidney.
drugs.source: DEMO fixture (not a validated drug database)

drugs.name: metformin
drugs.summary: DEMO RECORD. Oral agent used in type 2 diabetes. Relevant to CKD because it is described as renally cleared, so general references describe review against a person's level of kidney function, with use described as not recommended below a certain level.
drugs.source: DEMO fixture (not a validated drug database)

drugs.name: warfarin
drugs.summary: DEMO RECORD. Oral anticoagulant with a narrow therapeutic index, conventionally monitored using INR under clinician supervision. Included because bleeding risk and anticoagulation are commonly discussed alongside kidney disease.
drugs.source: DEMO fixture (not a validated drug database)

interactions.interaction: DEMO RECORD. Combining an ACE inhibitor with an NSAID is commonly described as reducing kidney perfusion and increasing the risk of acute kidney injury and raised potassium, particularly in CKD or where a person is volume-depleted.
interactions.mechanism: The ACE inhibitor is described as reducing efferent arteriolar tone while the NSAID is described as reducing prostaglandin-supported afferent blood flow, removing compensation on both sides of the glomerulus.
interactions.management: Demo placeholder: whether this combination is appropriate, and any alternative analgesic approach, is a decision for the treating clinician or pharmacist.
interactions.source: DEMO fixture (not a validated interaction database)

interactions.interaction: DEMO RECORD. Combining an ARB with an NSAID is described with the same concern as for ACE inhibitors: reduced kidney perfusion, raised potassium, and an increased chance of acute deterioration in CKD.
interactions.mechanism: ARBs act on the same renin-angiotensin system as ACE inhibitors, so the described NSAID concern applies to both classes.
interactions.management: Demo placeholder: discuss any NSAID use with a clinician or pharmacist before starting, including over-the-counter products.
interactions.source: DEMO fixture (not a validated interaction database)

interactions.interaction: DEMO RECORD. Using an ACE inhibitor together with an ARB is described as dual blockade of the renin-angiotensin system. General references describe increased rates of raised potassium, low blood pressure and acute kidney injury without an offsetting benefit, and describe routine combined use as something to avoid outside specialist circumstances.
interactions.mechanism: Both agents act on the same renin-angiotensin system at different points, so effects on potassium, blood pressure and glomerular filtration pressure are described as additive rather than complementary.
interactions.management: Demo placeholder: dual RAS blockade is a specialist decision and is not a routine combination.
interactions.source: DEMO fixture (not a validated interaction database)

interactions.interaction: DEMO RECORD. An ACE inhibitor combined with a loop diuretic is described as a recognised pairing that requires monitoring, because diuretic-induced volume depletion reduces the kidney's ability to maintain filtration once the renin-angiotensin system is blocked. This pair forms two thirds of the combination general references informally call the 'triple whammy'; adding an NSAID is described as completing it.
interactions.mechanism: The diuretic is described as reducing circulating volume while the ACE inhibitor is described as reducing the compensatory response that would otherwise maintain glomerular filtration pressure.
interactions.management: Demo placeholder: general references describe clinician monitoring of kidney function and electrolytes, and individualised advice about acute illness. Any such plan must come from the treating clinician.
interactions.source: DEMO fixture (not a validated interaction database)

interactions.interaction: DEMO RECORD. An ARB combined with a loop diuretic carries the same described concern as the ACE inhibitor pairing: volume depletion from the diuretic together with blockade of the renin-angiotensin system reduces the kidney's capacity to compensate. With an NSAID added, general references describe this as the 'triple whammy'.
interactions.mechanism: Reduced circulating volume from the diuretic combined with reduced angiotensin-mediated maintenance of glomerular filtration pressure.
interactions.management: Demo placeholder: monitoring and any sick-day plan are individualised clinical decisions.
interactions.source: DEMO fixture (not a validated interaction database)

interactions.interaction: DEMO RECORD. An NSAID combined with a loop diuretic is described as reducing the diuretic's effect and as contributing to fluid retention and reduced kidney perfusion. It is the third pairwise relationship within the combination general references call the 'triple whammy'.
interactions.mechanism: NSAID-mediated reduction in prostaglandin production is described as both blunting the diuretic response and reducing blood flow into the glomerulus.
interactions.management: Demo placeholder: discuss NSAID use with a clinician or pharmacist, including over-the-counter products.
interactions.source: DEMO fixture (not a validated interaction database)

interactions.interaction: DEMO RECORD. Concurrent use is widely described as increasing bleeding risk relative to either agent alone.
interactions.mechanism: Additive effects on haemostasis (anticoagulation plus NSAID platelet and gastric mucosal effects).
interactions.management: Demo placeholder: co-prescription decisions belong to the treating clinician.

dosage_reference.indication: type 2 diabetes mellitus in chronic kidney disease
dosage_reference.reference_text: DEMO REFERENCE TEXT ONLY - no numeric dose stored, consult clinician. General references describe metformin as renally cleared, with dose review against the person's level of kidney function and with use described as not recommended below a certain level of function. Temporary withholding during acute illness with dehydration and around iodinated contrast procedures is also commonly described. The specific decision is individualised; consult the prescribing clinician and the official product label.
